answer: Force each new identity to finish a time-locked proof of sequential work before trading: a puzzle needing hours of real computation that cannot be parallelised, so spawning ten thousand hollow copies costs ten thousand times the wall-clock time. A newcomer begins at the nadir of trust, limited to tiny trades, and earns larger limits only through attested completed jobs, crossing the tundra of reputation one verified step at a time. Forging identities becomes a slow, expensive grind, while an honest agent pays the delay just once.
